 2. AFTER, and this is the half that catches the race: `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` and READ EVERY PATH. A path you did not add means you reverted it; restore from disk, which still holds their version. Also read the DELETION COUNT rather than the exit code.
I ran step 2 on all ten of my commits this session; it caught the one clobber within a minute.

A lane following this item's own advice ("confirm the staged stat lists ONLY your paths") is protected; a lane that merely greps `^D` is NOT.

I support ajcr-p4's suggestion that the fresh-index sequence become a HUMAN-ISSUED protection rather than a lesson each lane rediscovers after clobbering someone -- three of my own r4 commits clobbered other lanes before I learned it.

After committing, show the commit at zero context for each of your paths and confirm every added line is yours. I did that on all three Lean files I touched this session.

    98	                (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))

   103	    (pic0FiniteStageFinalBaseChangeEquiv C L n m relation e M N
   104	        (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)).toAlgHom.comp

   106	          (R := N.1) (K := k)
   107	          (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   108	            (R := M.1) (K := N.1) (mapM q))) =

   120	    (phiL := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   121	      (R := M.1) (K := N.1) (mapM q))
   122	    (phiK := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   123	      (R := M.1) (K := k) (mapM q))

   130	    (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)).toAlgHom

   137	  let fN := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   138	    (R := N.1) (K := k)
   139	    (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   140	      (R := M.1) (K := N.1) (mapM q))
   141	  let fK := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   142	    (R := M.1) (K := k) (mapM q)

   145	  change eTarget.comp fK = g.comp eSource at hmodel

   148	    _ = eTarget.comp (cTarget.comp fN) := AlgHom.comp_assoc _ _ _
   149	    _ = eTarget.comp (fK.comp cSource) :=
   150	      congrArg (fun f => eTarget.comp f) hcancel

   152	    _ = (g.comp eSource).comp cSource :=
   153	      congrArg (fun f => f.comp cSource) hmodel
   154	    _ = g.comp (eSource.comp cSource) := AlgHom.comp_assoc _ _ _

     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The finite-stage Picard glue as a scheme over its field of definition
    10	
    11	The finite-stage glue package already contains affine algebras over its final finite
    12	subextension `P.N.1`.  Their structure maps agree on overlaps, so they descend to the
    13	glued scheme.  This retains the finite-stage object over `Spec P.N.1`, which is the
    14	object-level input for the scalar-extension comparison with the separably closed atlas.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
    22	open scoped TensorProduct
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    29	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    30	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    31	
    32	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    33	
    34	set_option linter.style.setOption false
    35	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    36	-- Projecting the dependent scalar towers from `P` requires a larger local synthesis budget.
    37	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    38	/-- The structure map from the finite-stage glued scheme to its field of definition. -/
    39	noncomputable def gluedMap
    40	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    41	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    42	    P.glueData.glued ⟶ Spec (.of P.N.1) := by
    43	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
    44	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
    45	  let A : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u := fun U =>
    46	    Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U
    47	  let B : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u :=
    48	    fun U V =>
    49	      Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V
    50	  let r : ∀ U V, A U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    51	    pic0FiniteStageRestrictionBaseChange
    52	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
    53	  letI : ∀ U V, Algebra (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    54	    pic0FiniteStageAlgebraOfMap (r U V)
    55	  letI : ∀ U V, IsScalarTower P.N.1 (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    56	    pic0FiniteStageTowerOfMap (r U V)
    57	  let tau : ∀ U V, B V U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    58	    pic0FiniteStageTransitionBaseChange
    59	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
    60	  fapply Multicoequalizer.desc
    61	  · intro U
    62	    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U
    63	    exact Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U)))
    64	  · rintro ⟨U, V⟩
    65	    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U V
    66	    change
    67	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A U) (B U V))) ≫
    68	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U))) =
    69	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (tau U V).toRingHom) ≫
    70	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A V) (B V U)))) ≫
    71	            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A V)))
    72	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    73	    rw [Category.assoc, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    74	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    75	    congr 1
    76	    ext x
    77	    simp only [CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, CommRingCat.hom_comp,
    78	      ConcreteCategory.hom_ofHom, RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply,
    79	      AlgHom.toRingHom_eq_coe, Category.assoc, RingHom.coe_coe]
    80	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A U) (B U V)]
    81	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A V) (B V U)]
    82	    exact (tau U V).commutes x |>.symm
    83	
    84	/-- The finite-stage Picard glue, retained over the finite field `P.N.1`. -/
    85	noncomputable def gluedOver
    86	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    87	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) : Over (Spec (.of P.N.1)) :=
    88	  Over.mk P.gluedMap
    89	
    90	end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    91	
    92	end
    93	
    94	end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	/-!
    11	# Affine intersections in the finite-stage Picard atlas
    12	
    13	The exact separably closed `Pic^0` representer is a group scheme over a field, hence is
    14	separated.  Consequently the intersection of any two affine charts in its chosen finite
    15	atlas is itself affine.  The canonical affine overlap packaged here is the geometric input
    16	for spreading out the finite atlas's restriction maps and gluing data.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    32	
    33	/-- The finite index type of charts in the chosen atlas of the exact separably closed
    34	`Pic^0` representer. -/
    35	abbrev Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex :=
    36	  { U // U ∈ (pic0FiniteStageAtlas C).charts }
    37	
    38	instance : Finite (Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :=
    39	  (pic0FiniteStageAtlas C).finite_charts.to_subtype
    40	
    41	/-- Pairwise intersections of charts in the chosen finite atlas of the exact separably
    42	closed `Pic^0` representer are affine.  This uses the group structure transported from
    43	the represented Picard functor, rather than adding separatedness as a hypothesis. -/
    44	theorem pic0FiniteStageAtlas_inter_isAffine
    45	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    46	    IsAffineOpen (U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1) := by
    47	  let J := (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1
    48	  letI : GrpObj J := (picRepDatumSepClosed C).grpObj
    49	  haveI : IsSeparated J.hom := isSeparated_of_grpObj J
    50	  haveI : Scheme.IsSeparated J.left := by
    51	    constructor
    52	    rw [← Limits.terminal.comp_from J.hom]
    53	    infer_instance
    54	  exact U.1.2.inf V.1.2
    55	
    56	/-- The intersection of two chosen finite-stage charts, regarded canonically as an affine
    57	open of the exact separably closed `Pic^0` representer. -/
    58	noncomputable def pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap
    59	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    60	    (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.affineOpens :=
    61	  ⟨U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1, pic0FiniteStageAtlas_inter_isAffine C U V⟩
    62	
    63	@[simp]
    64	theorem pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_open
    65	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    66	    (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).1 = U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1 :=
    67	  rfl
    68	
    69	/-- The canonical affine overlap is contained in its left chart. -/
    70	theorem pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_le_left
    71	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    72	    (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).1 ≤ U.1.1 :=
    73	  inf_le_left
    74	
    75	/-- The canonical affine overlap is contained in its right chart. -/
    76	theorem pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_le_right
    77	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    78	    (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).1 ≤ V.1.1 :=
    79	  inf_le_right
    80	
    81	/-! ## The canonical finite affine gluing datum -/
    82	
    83	/-- The chosen finite atlas as an actual open cover of the exact separably closed `Pic^0`
    84	representer. -/
    85	noncomputable def pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover :
    86	    (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.OpenCover :=
    87	  (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.openCoverOfIsOpenCover
    88	    (fun U : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C => U.1.1) (by
    89	      apply TopologicalSpace.IsOpenCover.mk
    90	      rw [iSup_subtype'']
    91	      exact (pic0FiniteStageAtlas C).iSup_opens)
    92	
    93	/-- Every object of the chosen finite open cover is affine. -/
    94	instance pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover_isAffine (U : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    95	    IsAffine ((pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).X U) := by
    96	  change IsAffine U.1.1.toScheme
    97	  exact U.1.2
    98	
    99	/-- The canonical finite affine gluing datum associated by Mathlib to the chosen open cover.
   100	Its transition maps and triple-overlap cocycle are construction output of `gluedCover`; this
   101	does not yet assert that the datum descends to a finite subextension. -/
   102	noncomputable def pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData : Scheme.GlueData :=
   103	  (pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).gluedCover
   104	
   105	/-- Every pairwise overlap scheme in the canonical finite gluing datum is affine. -/
   106	instance isAffine_pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData_V
   107	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
   108	    IsAffine ((pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData C).V (U, V)) := by
   109	  letI : IsAffine (U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1).toScheme :=
   110	    pic0FiniteStageAtlas_inter_isAffine C U V
   111	  let h := isPullback_opens_inf U.1.1 V.1.1
   112	  change IsAffine
   113	    (pullback ((pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).f U)
   114	      ((pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).f V))
   115	  change IsAffine (pullback U.1.1.ι V.1.1.ι)
   116	  exact IsAffine.of_isIso h.isoPullback.inv
   117	
   118	end
   119	
   120	end AlgebraicGeometry

## General Rules
- All line and column numbers are 1-indexed. Columns count characters (codepoints).
- This MCP does NOT edit files. Use other tools for editing.

## Key Tools
- **lean_goal**: Proof state at position. Omit `column` for before/after. `status` field: 'goals', 'complete' (proof done here), or 'no_goal_at_position' (not inside a proof).
- **lean_diagnostic_messages**: Compiler errors/warnings. "no goals to be solved" = remove tactics.
- **lean_term_goal**: Expected type at a position.
- **lean_hover_info**: Type signature + docs. Column at START of identifier.
- **lean_completions**: IDE autocomplete on incomplete code.
- **lean_local_search**: Fast local declaration search. Use BEFORE trying a lemma name.
- **lean_file_outline**: Token-efficient file skeleton (slow-ish).
- **lean_multi_attempt**: Test tactics without editing at a proof position. Use `column` for an exact source position; omit it for fast line-based attempts: `["simp", "ring", "omega"]`
- **lean_code_actions**: Quick fixes and `TryThis` suggestions (simp?, exact?) with resolved edits.
- **lean_declaration_file**: Declaration source slice with context; `full_file=true` for the whole file (large).
- **lean_references**: All usages of a symbol (capped by `max_results`, `total` reports the full count).
- **lean_run_code**: Run standalone snippet. Must include imports.
- **lean_verify**: Axiom check + source scan. Use fully qualified name (e.g. `Ns.thm`).
- **lean_minimal_hypotheses**: Which explicit hypotheses of a theorem are actually needed.
- **lean_build**: Run `lake build` + restart LSP. Only if needed (new imports). Use `fetch_cache=true` only for missing dependency caches. SLOW!
- **lean_profile_proof**: Profile a theorem for performance. Shows tactic hotspots. SLOW!

## Search Tools (rate limited)
- **lean_leansearch** (90/30s): Natural language -> mathlib
- **lean_loogle** (3/30s): Type pattern -> mathlib
- **lean_leanfinder** (10/30s): Semantic/conceptual search
- **lean_state_search** (6/30s): Goal -> closing lemmas
- **lean_hammer_premise** (6/30s): Goal -> premises for simp/aesop

## Search Decision Tree
1. "Does X exist locally?" -> lean_local_search
2. "I need a lemma that says X" -> lean_leansearch
3. "Find lemma with type pattern" -> lean_loogle
4. "What's the Lean name for concept X?" -> lean_leanfinder
5. "What closes this goal?" -> lean_state_search
6. "What to feed simp?" -> lean_hammer_premise

After finding a name: lean_local_search to verify, lean_hover_info for signature.

## Return Formats
List-returning tools return an object with an `items` array. Empty = `{"items": []}`.

## Slow Files
On large files, pass `timeout_s` to lean_diagnostic_messages / lean_goal. A
response with `partial: true` + `still_elaborating_lines` (or goal `status:
'still_elaborating'`) means Lean is still working - poll again; it is NOT an
error or a dead server.

## Error Handling
Check `isError` in responses: `true` means failure (timeout/LSP error/rate limit), while an empty `items` with `isError: false` means no results found.

Check theorem axioms + optional source scan. Only scans the given file, not imports.
